content: Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE) measures buoyant energy in air parcels. CAPE < 1000 J/kg represents marginal instability; 1000-2500 J/kg represents moderate-to-high instability capable of producing strong thunderstorms and hailstorms; CAPE > 2500 J/kg indicates extreme instability capable of producing severe supercells, microbursts, and tornadic squalls. Convective Inhibition (CIN) > 100 J/kg acts as a convective cap preventing storm initiation until surface heating or frontal lifting breaks the cap.

topic: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) Heat Action Protocol
content: NDMA Heat Action Plan specifies three color alert triggers: Yellow Alert (Hot day advisory, 40-42.9°C) - Keep public informed; Orange Alert (Heatwave warning, 43-44.9°C) - Open public shaded shelters, adjust school/work hours, mobilize oral rehydration centers in rural haats and bus stands; Red Alert (Extreme heat, >= 45°C) - Prohibit outdoor physical work 12 PM-4 PM, alert hospitals for emergency heatstroke triage, ensure water tankers in vulnerable settlements.
